clue.text: He always cleared his plate, but never got fat

definitions.text: He always cleared his plate, but never got fat

parts.words: He always cleared his plate, but never got fat
parts.note: a nursery-rhyme man who could eat no fat while his wife could eat no lean, so between them they licked the platter clean

explanation.surface: A description of a lean man with a hearty appetite who somehow never puts on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme says this man could eat no fat and his wife could eat no lean; together they cleared the plate. The clue reads like a dieting puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure in the English nursery rhyme is famous for eating only lean meat and leaving nothing behind.

clue.text: Not a fully-rounded national heroine?

parts.note: an arc is only part of a circle, so a heroine named after one is not fully rounded; the French national heroine burnt in 1431

explanation.surface: A question about whether a celebrated patriotic woman had a balanced personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fully-rounded' suggests character, but it is geometry: an arc is part of a circle, never the whole of one. The question mark flags the pun on the French heroine's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maid of Orleans is the national heroine of France, and her surname contains the word for part of a circle.

clue.text: Handled yacht soundly in rough

indicators.note: soundly here means said out loud, so the word for handling a yacht is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to handle a yacht as its sailors is to have crewed it

explanation.surface: A sailor coped well with a boat in stormy conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like praise for the handling, but it signals a homophone: CREWED said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough and unrefined are synonyms, as in a rough or unpolished sketch.

clue.text: Convenient set of rooms in which lab can work

indicators.note: in which says the next piece goes inside the set of rooms

parts.note: a suite is a set of rooms, as in a hotel

indicators.note: can work suggests the letters of lab may be worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Describing handy accommodation where a laboratory could operate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can work' is the anagram signal, and 'in which' is the container signal; 'Convenient' looks like a description of the rooms but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something convenient is fitting or appropriate for the purpose, a synonym.

clue.text: Took journey — notices I come in to land just off the tarmac

indicators.note: come in to means these letters enter the word for took a journey

parts.note: to have ridden somewhere is to have taken a journey
notices are advertisements, ADS

explanation.surface: A traveller describing an aircraft arriving just beside the runway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come in to land' reads as one aviation phrase, but 'come in to' is the container signal and 'land' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The strip of ground beside a road is the verge, land lying just off the tarmac surface.

clue.text: Tiara, initially pope's headgear

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word tiara

parts.note: Urban is the name of several popes

explanation.surface: A papal tiara described as the pontiff's special hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiara' looks like the headgear in question, but it only gives its first letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: A wound cloth head covering is a kind of hat, so it counts as headgear.

clue.text: Try to spot man expected on stage

parts.note: to have a go is to try
a dot is a spot

explanation.surface: Someone attempting to catch sight of a performer due to appear.
explanation.walkthrough: In Beckett's play two tramps wait for this man, who never arrives on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Beckett's play is awaited throughout but never appears on stage.

clue.text: Drinking vessel allowed to slip under mouth.

indicators.note: to slip under places this piece below the other in the down light

parts.note: gob is a slang word for mouth
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A cup someone was permitted to let fall from their lips.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, a piece that slips under another is written after it; 'to slip under' is that placement signal. Gob is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A stemmed wine glass or cup is a vessel for drinking from.

clue.text: Yanks touring part of Arabia found guides

indicators.note: touring means going around, so drags encircles the country

parts.note: to yank is to drag, so yanks means drags
Oman is a country in the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: Americans travelling through the Middle East discovered local guides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yanks' looks like Americans, but it is the verb; 'touring' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: These were interpreters and guides in Arabic-, Turkish- or Persian-speaking countries.

clue.text: From deep dish, take out first of unusual wooden objects

indicators.note: take out says to remove a letter from the dish

parts.note: a tureen is a deep dish for serving soup

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of unusual

explanation.surface: Instructions to remove odd wooden items from a serving bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take out' removes U, the first letter of 'unusual', from TUREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Treen is a collective term for small handmade wooden household items.

clue.text: A famous person removing lines finally used emery

indicators.note: removing takes the following letters out of the famous person

parts.note: a luminary is a famous or eminent person
RY, short for railway, is the usual crossword abbreviation for lines

explanation.surface: A celebrity sanded something down after cutting out their lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removing' is the deletion signal and 'finally' says the lines come off the end of the famous person; emery is mostly aluminium oxide.
explanation.definitionFit: Emery is a natural abrasive consisting largely of aluminium oxide, so it is loosely this compound.

clue.text: Set of bones found in chest

definitions.text: Set of bones found in chest

parts.words: Set of bones found in chest
parts.note: suggests a skeleton in a box, but chest here is the human torso and the bones enclose it

explanation.surface: A grisly discovery of a skeleton inside a storage trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: A chest sounds like a trunk, but it is the torso, enclosed by the ring of curved bones.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved bones enclosing the thorax form a protective structure around heart and lungs.

clue.text: A great beauty's love rejected in letter

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the whole run is read in reverse

parts.note: a gem is a person or thing of great beauty
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A gorgeous woman's affections spurned in a written message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' reverses A + GEM + O as one run. 'Letter' is a Greek letter, not a message.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the last letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Overcharge villainously for improvised bed

definitions.meaning: to extort money by force or fraud, a racket
a makeshift bed, made up on the floor

explanation.surface: A crook charging too much for a makeshift bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an extortion racket and a temporary bed made up wherever is handy.

clue.text: Praise officer that's broken a rebel leader

indicators.note: that's broken says the officer has broken into the next word

parts.note: Jack Cade led the Kentish rebellion of 1450
COL is the abbreviation for colonel

explanation.surface: Commending a military man who defeated an insurgent chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's broken' signals the officer breaking into the rebel's name. Jack Cade led a 1450 English peasant revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: An award or expression of high praise is a synonym, as in winning critical plaudits.

clue.text: Perplexity in study on nuclear reaction

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
fusion is a nuclear reaction joining atomic nuclei

explanation.surface: Being baffled while researching a physics process.
explanation.walkthrough: CON for study is an old usage still common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Perplexity and bewilderment are synonyms, being unable to understand.

clue.text: Landowner not allowed to finish enclosure

indicators.note: not allowed to finish means the landowner loses his last letter

parts.note: a laird is a Scottish landowner

explanation.surface: A property owner barred from completing a fenced area.
explanation.walkthrough: A LAIRD is the Scottish word for an estate owner; dropping the final D leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's den is a sheltered enclosed place where it lives.

clue.text: You'll bear moving in the — shade

indicators.note: moving says the letters are moved into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An invitation to relocate into a particular colour scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash in the clue stands for the answer: 'in the royal blue shade'. 'Moving' rearranges YOULLBEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep vivid blue colour is one shade of the colour spectrum.

clue.text: Old sailors' guide has page on bunting

parts.note: the ortolan is a small European bunting, a songbird

explanation.surface: A navigation book containing a page about flags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunting' suggests flags, but here it is the bird. In a down clue, 'on' puts P above ORTOLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval sailing charts and directions for ports were called by this name.

clue.text: Little woman majestic? Not seriously

parts.note: Jo March is one of the sisters in Little Women
kingly means regal or majestic

explanation.surface: A small lady asking if she is regal, but only in fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little woman' points to Jo, from Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in jest is doing it without seriousness, a synonym.

clue.text: Element of geometry children can lick

definitions.meaning: a solid figure tapering from a round base to a point
the wafer holder for an ice cream

explanation.surface: A geometry lesson that children can eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a tapering solid in geometry and a wafer cup holding ice cream.

clue.text: Island settlement holds appeal

indicators.note: holds means the settlement contains the next piece

parts.note: a colony is a settlement
SA is short for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A colonial island outpost has a certain charm.
explanation.walkthrough: COLONY holds SA. COLONSAY is an island of the Inner Hebrides off Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonsay is a small island in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland.

clue.text: Split stick

definitions.meaning: to split apart, as with an axe

explanation.definitionFit: This is a contronym meaning both to divide apart and to adhere closely.

clue.text: Extensive raised area provided to support crowd

indicators.note: to support places this piece underneath the crowd in a down light

parts.note: a mass is a crowd
if means provided that

explanation.surface: A large platform built so that it could bear the weight of many people.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, a piece that supports another sits below it, so 'to support' is the placement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact mountainous block forming a raised upland mass is the geographical term.

clue.text: Partnership could abet criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests the words are bent out of shape

explanation.surface: A partner in crime may help with an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges COULDABET.
explanation.definitionFit: Two performers working together on stage form a partnership.

clue.text: Choice of colour last month — gold

parts.note: December is the last month, DEC
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Picking paint last month and going for gold.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic term for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The decorative scheme of a room includes its colours and furnishings.

clue.text: Drive, taking fast road back, and parking by city railroad

indicators.note: back means the motorway name is reversed

parts.note: the M1 is the main motorway north from London, a fast road
P is the sign for parking
the El is an elevated railroad in an American city such as Chicago

explanation.surface: A motorist reversing on the motorway and parking beside a city railway.
explanation.walkthrough: M1, Britain's first motorway, written MI and reversed, gives IM. EL is the elevated railway of Chicago.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or urge forward, a synonym.

clue.text: Hellish leader represented as cartoon character

definitions.meaning: the Roman god ruling the underworld
Mickey Mouse's pet dog in Disney cartoons

explanation.surface: A demonic chief drawn as a figure in an animated film.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the Roman ruler of the underworld and to a Disney cartoon dog.

clue.text: Fool put on strange-sounding body armour

indicators.note: put on places the fool after the other piece
sounding means the word for strange is heard, not spelt

parts.note: queer in its old sense means strange
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: An idiot donned oddly named protective gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange-sounding' looks like a description of the armour's name, but QUEER said aloud gives CUIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A breastplate and backplate fastened together form a piece of body armour.

clue.text: From a fast one, stroke on one side of wicket

indicators.note: on says this piece follows the other in the across light

parts.note: leg is the leg side of the cricket field, beside the batsman's legs
a pull is a cricket stroke hitting the ball to the leg side

explanation.surface: A batsman playing a stroke to the leg side off a fast bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A fast one' sounds like a fast ball, but it is a trick, as in pulling a fast one. In cricket the LEG side is behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling a fast one is a deception, and a hoax played on someone is a synonym.

clue.text: Travelled round north for a dance

indicators.note: round means the travelled word circles the next piece

parts.note: rode means travelled, on horseback or by vehicle

explanation.surface: A journey around the north to attend a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: RODE goes round N.
explanation.definitionFit: A ronde is a round dance, from the French word for round.

clue.text: Curious type of blood a person's found in part of arm

parts.note: funny means odd or curious
B is a blood group
one means a person, as in one does

explanation.surface: An odd blood group belonging to someone was discovered in their limb.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'person's' is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The elbow spot where the ulnar nerve tingles when knocked is called this.
